name: Shark Bay
notes: East Santo language of the Shark Bay area. All three POc bilabials have dental reflexes before *i, *e, *a: *m > n, *b > t, *p > θ (Lynch 2005b: 399-400, Tables 2-3). Lynch (2019a: 304, Table 4) lists it as 'Shark Bay II', with apical reflexes, and groups Shark Bay I, Shark Bay II and Lorediakarkar as 'Shark Bay'; which of Tryon's (1976) lists the 2005 'Shark Bay' is, is not said there. Lynch's data are Guy's (1978) and Tryon's (1976) and 'there is not much information available on any of these languages' (2005b: 399). The reflexes are stated against POc, so the lect is entered under POc and listed under Northern Vanuatu (tree_parent), as Nese is under Central Vanuatu. Glottocode, ISO code and coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023: 628).
inherit_note: Lynch states only the reflexes of POc *m, *b and *p (Table 3); the other phonemes are assumed unchanged from POc, which is certainly too little.

name: Tolomako
notes: Espiritu Santo. POc *m and *b have the dental reflexes n and t before *i, *e, *a, but *p is v everywhere (Lynch 2005b: 399-400, Tables 2-3; 2019a: 304, Table 4, 'does not apply to *p'). Guy (1978: 783) has two dialects: the shift 'occurs in the Tolomako dialect, but there is no evidence of it at all in the Tsureviu dialect, where *m, *b and *p are reflected as m, p and v in all environments' (Lynch 2005b: 399, n. 11); the rows are the Tolomako dialect, and Tsureviu is not a lect. Lynch (2019a: 320): the only language of the lexicostatistical West Santo group with the shift, an outlier in it, which 'may be classifiable as an East Santo language'. Lynch's data are Guy's (1978) and Tryon's (1976) and 'there is not much information available on any of these languages' (2005b: 399). The reflexes are stated against POc, so the lect is entered under POc and listed under Northern Vanuatu (tree_parent), as Nese is under Central Vanuatu.
